about.description:
LCM is a set of libraries and tools for message passing and data
marshalling, targeted at real-time systems where high-bandwidth and low
latency are critical. It provides a publish/subscribe message passing
model and automatic marshalling/unmarshalling code generation with
bindings for applications in a variety of programming languages.

liblcm contains the shared C/C++ library and the lcm-gen, lcm-logger and
lcm-logplayer tools; liblcm-devel contains the headers and the CMake and
pkg-config files; lcm contains the Python bindings.

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "1.5.3"

recipe:
  name: lcm
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/lcm-proj/lcm/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: f7e693d50e229e37de00387ac8ab9228e16559dd57bddd155c4b5ca1c233834e
  patches:
    # Build only the shared liblcm; lcm-static becomes an alias of it (in-tree
    # and in the installed lcmConfig.cmake), so nothing links a static library.
    - 0001-build-shared-library-only.patch
    # fdatasync() is not declared by the macOS SDK; use fsync() there
    - 0002-use-fsync-on-macos.patch
    # Allow building lcm-python on its own against an installed lcm
    # (find_package(lcm)), fix its Windows install path, optionally install a
    # .dist-info, and let lcm.run_script() find the tools in the conda layout.
    - 0003-python-standalone-build.patch

build:
  number: 0

outputs:
  - staging:
      name: lcm-build
    build:
      script: build_liblcm
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - cmake
        - ninja
        - pkg-config
      host:
        - glib

  - package:
      name: liblcm
    inherit: lcm-build
    build:
      files:
        - if: unix
          then:
            - lib/liblcm.so.*
            - lib/liblcm.*.dylib
            - bin/lcm-gen
            - bin/lcm-logger
            - bin/lcm-logplayer
            - share/man/man1/lcm-*.1
          else:
            - Library/bin/lcm.dll
            - Library/bin/lcm-gen.exe
            - Library/bin/lcm-logger.exe
            - Library/bin/lcm-logplayer.exe
            - Library/share/man/man1/lcm-*.1
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          bin:
            - lcm-gen
            - lcm-logger
            - lcm-logplayer
          files:
            exists:
              - if: linux
                then:
                  - lib/liblcm.so.1
              - if: osx
                then:
                  - lib/liblcm.1.dylib
              - if: win
                then:
                  - Library/bin/lcm.dll
            not_exists:
              - if: unix
                then:
                  - include/**
                  - lib/liblcm.a
                  - lib/liblcm.so
                  - lib/liblcm.dylib
                else:
                  - Library/include/**
                  - Library/lib/*.lib
      - script:
          - lcm-gen --version
          - lcm-gen --help

  - package:
      name: liblcm-devel
    inherit: lcm-build
    build:
      files:
        - if: unix
          then:
            - include/lcm/**
            - lib/liblcm.so
            - lib/liblcm.dylib
            - lib/lcm/cmake/**
            - lib/pkgconfig/lcm.pc
          else:
            - Library/include/lcm/**
            - Library/lib/lcm.lib
            - Library/CMake/lcm*.cmake
            - Library/lib/pkgconfig/lcm.pc
    requirements:
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('liblcm', exact=True) }}
        # lcm.pc has `Requires: glib-2.0`
        - glib
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('liblcm', upper_bound='x.x') }}
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          include:
            - lcm/lcm.h
            - lcm/lcm-cpp.hpp
            - lcm/lcm_coretypes.h
            - lcm/lcm_export.h
            - lcm/eventlog.h
          files:
            exists:
              - if: linux
                then:
                  - lib/liblcm.so
              - if: osx
                then:
                  - lib/liblcm.dylib
              - if: unix
                then:
                  - lib/lcm/cmake/lcmConfig.cmake
                  - lib/lcm/cmake/lcmConfigVersion.cmake
                  - lib/lcm/cmake/lcmTargets.cmake
                  - lib/lcm/cmake/lcmUtilities.cmake
                  - lib/pkgconfig/lcm.pc
                else:
                  - Library/lib/lcm.lib
                  - Library/CMake/lcmConfig.cmake
                  - Library/CMake/lcmConfigVersion.cmake
                  - Library/CMake/lcmTargets.cmake
                  - Library/CMake/lcmUtilities.cmake
                  - Library/lib/pkgconfig/lcm.pc
            # no static library is built or shipped
            not_exists:
              - if: unix
                then:
                  - lib/liblcm.a
                  - lib/liblcm-static.a
                else:
                  - Library/lib/lcm-static.lib
      - files:
          recipe:
            - test/CMakeLists.txt
            - test/example_t.lcm
            - test/test_c.c
            - test/test_cpp.cpp
        requirements:
          run:
            - ${{ compiler('c') }}
            - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
            - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
            - cmake
            - ninja
            - pkg-config
        script:
          - pkg-config --exists --print-errors lcm
          - pkg-config --cflags --libs lcm
          - if: unix
            then:
              - cmake -S test -B build -G Ninja ${CMAKE_ARGS} -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
              - cmake --build build
              - ./build/test_c
              - ./build/test_cpp
            else:
              - cmake -S test -B build -G Ninja %CMAKE_ARGS% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
              - cmake --build build
              - .\build\test_c.exe
              - .\build\test_cpp.exe

  - package:
      name: lcm
    build:
      script: build_lcm_python
    requirements:
      build:
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - python
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - cmake
        - ninja
      host:
        - python
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('liblcm-devel', exact=True) }}
      run:
        - python
        # also provides the lcm-gen, lcm-logger and lcm-logplayer tools that
        # lcm.run_script() wraps
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('liblcm', exact=True) }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - lcm
          pip_check: true
      - files:
          recipe:
            - test/test_python.py
            - test/example_t.lcm
        requirements:
          run:
            - python
        script:
          - python test/test_python.py

about:
  homepage: https://lcm-proj.github.io/lcm/
  repository: https://github.com/lcm-proj/lcm
  documentation: https://lcm-proj.github.io/lcm/
  summary: Lightweight Communications and Marshalling
  description: |
    LCM is a set of libraries and tools for message passing and data
    marshalling, targeted at real-time systems where high-bandwidth and low
    latency are critical. It provides a publish/subscribe message passing
    model and automatic marshalling/unmarshalling code generation with
    bindings for applications in a variety of programming languages.

    liblcm contains the shared C/C++ library and the lcm-gen, lcm-logger and
    lcm-logplayer tools; liblcm-devel contains the headers and the CMake and
    pkg-config files; lcm contains the Python bindings.
  # LCM itself is LGPL-2.1-or-later; on Windows the tools additionally link the
  # vendored BSD-3-Clause getopt implementation from WinSpecific/getopt.
  license: LGPL-2.1-or-later AND BSD-3-Clause
  license_file:
    - COPYING
    - WinSpecific/getopt/getopt.c

extra:
  feedstock-name: lcm
  recipe-maintainers:
    - Tobias-Fischer
